title: Reconnect
blurb: Rebuild closeness and non-sexual touch before anything else. Best after a busy or distant stretch.

weeks.lesson: Desire grows from feeling noticed. Before technique, rebuild small moments of full attention: phones away, eyes up.

ex.d: Kiss for a full six seconds, once a day, no agenda. Notice how your body responds.
Sit together, no screens. Each answers: "What was one good moment this week, and one thing I need?" The listener only reflects back.
Two minutes of silent eye contact. Laugh if you need to; that is part of it.

weeks.lesson: Touch that does not have to lead to sex lowers pressure and makes real desire easier. Agree "this is just for pleasure" out loud.

ex.d: Ten minutes each, slow, with oil or lotion. Receiver gives one line of feedback: warmer, softer, slower.
Choose a daily 10-minute cuddle position. Breathe together.
Run a Sweet-level guided session with the "Romantic" mood.

weeks.lesson: People open up where they feel admired. Specific praise beats general praise.

ex.d: Tell your partner three specific things you find attractive or loving about them, one of them physical.
Give each other a coupon for something small and thoughtful.
Write one journal entry about what felt good this week.

weeks.lesson: Playfulness keeps long relationships alive. Laughter and novelty are both intimacy.

ex.d: Send one flirty message in the day. Keep it kind and teasing.
Play Truth or Dare at Sweet level.
Plan one date for next week together, even a home one.

title: Talk About Sex
blurb: A gentle path to saying what you want, hearing what your partner wants, and handling "no" with warmth.

weeks.lesson: Many couples struggle simply because they have no comfortable words. Agree on words you both like (and words you dislike) first.

ex.d: Each lists words you like and dislike for body parts and acts. Compare.
Go through the private Match list on your own, then compare overlaps.
Browse the Kink Explorer together, only reacting with curiosity.

weeks.lesson: Use "I" statements and a specific request: "I'd love it if you… slowly" works better than "you never…".

ex.d: Each states three things you would love, framed positively. Partner repeats them back.
During a massage use only: "more / less / there / slower". Practise guiding.
Play Desire Match and discuss any surprise.

weeks.lesson: A "no" is information, not rejection. The best reply is "thank you for telling me", followed by an alternative.

ex.d: Take turns asking for something small; the other practises a kind no plus an alternative.
Choose a safeword and a slow-down word. Practise using each once.
Read the consent and aftercare guide together.

weeks.lesson: A short, kind debrief after intimacy ("what did you love? anything to change?") builds trust faster than anything else.

ex.d: After your next intimate time, 10 minutes of cuddling plus one thing you loved each.
Record the night in your journal with a rating.
Do the weekly Pulse and compare.

title: Desire & Rhythm
blurb: For couples with mismatched desire or a routine that has gone quiet. Practical, pressure-free.

weeks.lesson: Some people feel desire first (spontaneous); many feel it only after touch begins (responsive). Neither is wrong; plan for both.

ex.d: Each notes when, where and with what you feel most open (time of day, mood, setting).
Look at your Pulse trends and talk about patterns.
Discuss: when does sex feel like an obligation? What would remove that?

weeks.lesson: Anticipation is the cheapest and strongest aphrodisiac. Teasing earlier in the day makes the evening easier.

ex.d: Send a message in the morning about what you would like tonight.
Send a secret envelope with a small dare.
Put one date night in your calendars.

weeks.lesson: Novelty can be tiny: a new room, time, or order of touch.

ex.d: Do things in a different order than usual: massage first, kissing later.
Try a short roleplay scene.
Draw three tasks from a pack you both picked.

weeks.lesson: Couples who plan intimacy keep it. Planning is not unromantic; it is care.

ex.d: Pick a regular "us" time and guard it.
Keep the streak by doing something small together each day.
Look at your History and talk about what worked best.

title: Long-Distance Intimacy
blurb: Stay close across time zones using the Together tools: messages, shared games and check-ins.

weeks.lesson: Small frequent contact beats rare long calls. Predictable rituals create safety across distance.

ex.d: Link your accounts in Together.
Send a short note each day for a week in Chat.

ex.t: Share a photo of your day
ex.d: Something ordinary: your coffee, your view.

weeks.lesson: Doing the same activity at the same time makes distance feel smaller.

ex.d: Draw a shared card live while on a call.
Pick a song; listen together and message what you feel.
Choose a film and chat during it.

weeks.lesson: Agree boundaries first: what is okay on camera, what is only text, what stays private. Never record or screenshot without clear consent.

ex.d: Use the Match tool to find what you both like.
Write a short scene for your partner, read it aloud by call.
Start a shared timer and each do a slow self-touch or breathing exercise, then compare notes.

weeks.lesson: Anticipation of the next meeting keeps desire alive.

ex.d: Each writes 5 things you want to do at your next meeting.
Open a secret envelope together on a call.
Add shared bucket list items.

title: Beginner Kink, Safely
blurb: Explore power play and sensation with consent, negotiation and aftercare built in.

weeks.lesson: Negotiate before, not during. Cover wants, limits, safeword, health, and how you will check in.

ex.d: Read the consent and aftercare section together.
Complete the match list; only talk about overlaps.
Set stop and slow words and practise each.

weeks.lesson: Start soft: touch, temperature, light scratching, blindfold. Slow progress, frequent check-ins.

ex.d: One partner receives with a blindfold; the other uses feather, fingertips, warm breath.
Try tasks from a sensory or light-bondage pack.
Complete a step from the Journey.

weeks.lesson: Power play is trust made visible. The "bottom" has the real control through limits and the safeword.

ex.d: Agree a short scene where one leads; end with aftercare.
Plan a scene together.
Do a challenge step.

weeks.lesson: Both partners can feel emotionally low after intense play ("drop"). Plan warmth, water, food and talk for the next day.

ex.d: Prepare blanket, water, snack, something soft for next time.
Message the day after: how are you feeling, body and mind?
Update your yes/maybe/no list and log the experience.
